campaign_truths.recommended_action: Increase daily budget — this product delivers $2.94 in contribution profit per dollar spent with 94 days of healthy inventory.
Reduce spend immediately — a 22% return rate and 38% gross margin mean every ad dollar returns less than $1.00 in contribution profit.
Reduce spend to protect working capital — inventory will be exhausted in 12 days and scaling now creates stockout exposure before replenishment arrives.
Maintain current spend — product generates solid contribution margin with stable inventory and no operational risk.
Significantly increase daily budget — the Starter Bundle generates $5.01 in contribution profit per ad dollar, the highest return in the portfolio, yet receives the lowest spend allocation.

audit.top_anomaly_summary: Hydrating Cleanser is the portfolio's worst performer despite showing the highest reported ROAS of 5.1x: after factoring in a 22% return rate, 38% gross margin, and fulfillment costs, it generates only $0.99 in contribution profit per ad dollar — a net loss position. Simultaneously, the Starter Bundle delivers $5.01 in contribution profit per ad dollar but receives just $95/day, the lowest budget in the entire portfolio.

reallocation.constraint_summary: Retinol Night Cream spend was reduced due to confirmed 12-day stockout risk, preventing further inventory depletion ahead of replenishment. Hydrating Cleanser was not increased per the brand constraint; spend was reduced to halt contribution margin losses.

budget_moves.rationale: This product delivers $2.94 in contribution profit per ad dollar with 94 days of healthy inventory — reallocating freed budget here directly increases weekly contribution margin without operational risk.
A 22% return rate and 38% gross margin mean this campaign returns only $0.99 in contribution profit per ad dollar — continuing at $420/day accelerates net losses of approximately $210 per week.

With only 12 days of inventory remaining, scaling this product creates stockout risk and working capital exposure — a measured reduction preserves sell-through without compounding out-of-stock downside.

This campaign generates stable contribution margin at $2.02 per ad dollar with no operational risk — maintaining current spend preserves a reliable baseline while broader portfolio reallocation is absorbed.

The Starter Bundle produces $5.01 in contribution profit per ad dollar — the highest return in the portfolio — with 88 days of healthy inventory and a 4% return rate, making it the strongest candidate to convert freed budget into incremental weekly profit.

reallocation.executive_summary: By redirecting $290 per day away from an unprofitable cleanser campaign and a stockout-risk product toward the two highest-margin SKUs, weekly contribution profit is projected to increase by $2,388 with no change to total daily spend. This plan requires no additional budget — only a reallocation of existing resources toward products with proven contribution margin strength.

experiment.opportunity_rationale: The Starter Bundle is receiving the largest budget increase in this reallocation — $150/day — based on the highest contribution margin ratio in the portfolio at $5.01 per ad dollar. With 88 days of inventory, a 4% return rate, and an $89 average order value, this campaign has strong fundamentals that a creative optimization could amplify significantly. No brand constraint applies, and risk is low, making it the clear experiment candidate to validate whether the true profit improvement exceeds the conservative reallocation baseline.
experiment.hypothesis: If we replace the current product feature headline with a social proof headline featuring a verified five-star customer review, then conversion rate will increase by 10-15% because purchase intent for an $89 bundle is more sensitive to peer validation than product specification, and the Starter Bundle's 4% return rate signals high buyer satisfaction that is not currently surfaced in the ad creative.
experiment.control_description: Current ad set showing Starter Bundle product image with feature-based headline copy at $95/day spend targeting the existing audience segment.
experiment.variant_description: Same targeting and budget allocation, but headline replaced with the brand's highest-rated verified buyer quote alongside a value-anchor line quantifying the bundle saving versus purchasing items individually.
experiment.primary_success_metric: Contribution margin per 1,000 impressions (revenue per impression adjusted for return rate and gross margin)
experiment.secondary_success_metric: Product return rate — must not increase above 6% or the margin thesis weakens
experiment.minimum_detectable_effect: 10% lift in conversion rate at 80% statistical power
experiment.risk_assessment: Primary risk is a temporary conversion rate dip during creative ramp-up, but with a 50/50 split and 21-day window the maximum downside is capped before statistical significance is reached.
